source.title: Beyond scaling curves: internal dynamics of neural networks through the NTK lens
source.authors: Konstantin Nikolaou; Sven Krippendorf; S. Tovey; Daniel Fink

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests performance scaling in standard vision datasets, extending scaling-law analysis beyond language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The study reports loss scaling for vision tasks, not language-model pretraining. It does not test extrapolation to much larger runs or compute-optimal allocations. Prior-work results are cited, not cataloged as this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study trains small dense networks on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10. It reports its own test-loss power-law exponents for scaling width (100 training samples fixed) and dataset size (8-unit model fixed). This bears on V5 (power-law form in image models). The rest of the paper is NTK dynamics, which is a different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Loss scales as a power law with exponents of about 0.5 for both model and data size, yet NTK dynamics differ in opposite ways, so loss exponents alone are insufficient to understand the mechanism. The authors also identify a feature-to-kernel transition at widths of about 500–1000, more than ten times below LLM feed-forward widths, with depth affecting the transition.
record.recipe_differences: Uses small dense networks on standard vision datasets with cross-entropy loss, rather than language-model pretraining runs; studies model and dataset scaling, not language-model compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors note that their scaling exponent differs from the exponent reported by Bahri et al. (2024) and suggest different learning rates and initializations as possible causes.

fits_no_version.finding: Similar loss exponents for model and data scaling coincide with opposite NTK dynamics. Effective rank rises with width but falls with data size; width changes the initial trace, while data changes the trace adaptation rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Matching loss-scaling exponents do not imply the same internal learning mechanism.

fits_no_version.finding: The NTK trace ratio falls as a power law in width (exponent about -0.7 to -0.84). Effective rank rises as a power law and then plateaus at a feature-to-kernel transition near width 500 (MNIST, Fashion-MNIST) or 1000 (CIFAR-10).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Width scaling passes from a feature-driven to a kernel-driven regime at a finite width that depends on depth.

record.problems: Experiments focus on low-data and small-model regimes; the loss scaling results concern vision datasets rather than language-model pretraining. The paper says its setups did not reproduce the exponent 1.0 reported by Bahri et al. (2024), and suggests learning-rate or initialization differences may account for this.

untested.parts: No extrapolation from small to much larger runs.
Depth (3 vs 4 layers) is varied only for NTK quantities, not for loss at fixed parameter count.

Only small MLPs on small image-classification sets in the variance-limited regime, over about 2 orders of magnitude. No video, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer, and no large or resolution-limited regime.
No setup or fitting choice is varied. The gap with the exponent of 1.0 from Bahri et al. is noted only in a footnote, with the cause (learning rate, initialization) speculated, not tested.

record.verdict_notes: V7 is dropped from the rows. The only V7-relevant content is the footnote that the authors could not reproduce Bahri et al.'s exponent of 1.0 in a setup aligned with theirs, attributed speculatively to learning rate or initialization. This hints that exponents depend on setup, but the paper does not test it. The V5 support is narrow: tiny MLPs, a deliberately bottlenecked regime, and about 2 decades of width or data.

versions.untested_parts: Tests vision-task loss, not held-out language-model pretraining loss.
Does not fit laws on small runs and test predictions on runs orders of magnitude larger.
Does not compare parameter/token allocations at fixed compute or test their growth with compute.
Does not compare loss across depth, width, or other architectures at a fixed parameter count.
Tests standard vision datasets with dense networks; does not test other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Does not test downstream-task performance as a function of language-model pretraining loss or scale.
Notes a scaling-exponent discrepancy that may relate to learning rates and initialization; does not test parameter-counting choices, compute-optimal allocation, or systematic loss-curve bending.

relationships.condition: Small dense nets on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10; width scaling (100 samples) and data scaling (8-unit model), variance-limited regime
relationships.reason: Test loss follows a power law with exponents of about -0.45 to -0.54 across all three datasets and both axes (r1–r6).
relationships.display_finding: Test-loss power-law exponents ranged approximately from −0.45 to −0.54 across all three datasets and both width and data scaling.
